correctness.rationale: The three orbit types exhaust unordered pairs, with multiplicities 2m, m, 2m(m−1). Grounding preserves diagonal degrees and yields a positive definite matrix. Independently, set a=1+t, b=1+2t, p(s)=(1+s)(b+s). The shifted determinants for H,S,D are respectively (a+s)p(s)^(m−1), p(s)^(m−1)[2m+s−2(m−1)/(1+s)], and (a+s)^2 p(s)^(m−2)[2m+s−2/(a+s)−2(m−2)/(1+s)]. Each factor follows by petal splitting and scalar hub elimination. The negative second log derivative at zero is J₂; expanding these recovers both displayed orbit gaps exactly. The S gap is greater than 13/4, so S is never optimal. The D numerator has positive coefficients for m≥3 and reduces at m=2 to 13−14t−15t² with one positive root. This establishes the complete minimizers, including ties, and minimum. The first log derivative likewise gives the distinct J₁ gap; its S gap is (2m−1)/2−1/(1+t)>0. The disagreement intervals and the m=3,t=4 example follow. Modal Lyapunov equations for unit white acceleration noise give positional variance per eigenmode 1/(2γδλ²), consistent with the stated normalization.
residual_risks: Exactly two perfectly grounded leaders, identical petals and common conductances, with unnormalized Laplacian. No conclusion for finite gains, heterogeneous weights or other noise models.

value.rationale: An exact optimizer for a standard noisy second-order consensus criterion on a natural weighted graph gives a sharp counterexample to transferring first-order leader rules. The switch exists only on five vertices, and a conductance-driven switch for the first-inverse objective persists on seven vertices precisely where the second-order objective never switches. The all-size orbit classification, including ties, is useful as a benchmark beyond an isolated inverse computation.
residual_risks: Restricted graph family and damping/noise model; no generic leader placement principle inferred.
